questions.question: Given the two clauses ¬P(x) ∨ Q(x) and P(a) ∨ R, which clause can be derived by a single resolution step?
questions.explanation:
Resolving ¬P(x) ∨ Q(x) with P(a) ∨ R uses the complementary literals P(a) and ¬P(x) after the substitution {x/a}. The resolvent is Q(a) ∨ R, matching the resolution rule described on page 180.

questions.question: To apply Generalized Modus Ponens to the rule ∀x (Animal(x) ∧ HasTail(x) → Mammal(x)) and the fact HasTail(Fido), which most general unifier (MGU) is required?

options.D: No unifier is needed because the antecedent is already ground.

questions.explanation:
The antecedent Animal(x) ∧ HasTail(x) must match the known fact HasTail(Fido). Unifying x with Fido yields the substitution {x → Fido}, as explained in the unification discussion on page 4 (14:19).

questions.question: Which of the following sequences correctly converts the formula B ↔ (P ∨ Q) into conjunctive normal form (CNF)?

options.A: Eliminate ↔, then eliminate →, then distribute ∨ over ∧.
options.B: Eliminate →, then eliminate ↔, then move ¬ inward.
options.C: Eliminate ↔, eliminate →, move ¬ inward, then distribute ∧ over ∨.
options.D: Eliminate ↔, eliminate →, move ¬ inward, then distribute ∨ over ∧.

questions.explanation:
The CNF conversion steps listed on page 13:32 are: (1) eliminate ↔, (2) eliminate →, (3) push negations inward, (4) distribute ∨ over ∧ and flatten. Option D follows this order.

questions.question: In a Horn‑clause knowledge base, which inference rule should be used to derive a new atomic conclusion from the clause ¬A ∨ ¬B ∨ C and the facts A and B?
questions.explanation:
Horn clauses can be processed by forward chaining with Modus Ponens (or its generalized form). Given ¬A ∨ ¬B ∨ C (equivalently A ∧ B → C) and the facts A and B, forward chaining derives C, as noted on page 180 (Modus Ponens rule for Horn KBs).

questions.question: In a resolution refutation proof, the goal is to show that the KB ⊨ ¬P(a). After converting the KB to CNF, which additional clause must be added to start the refutation?
questions.explanation: To prove ¬P(a) by refutation, we add the negation of the goal, i.e., the clause P(a), to the set of CNF clauses and then derive a contradiction using resolution (page 180, resolution algorithm). The correct added clause is P(a).
